mappings.note: The IT industry's main source of foreign exchange is its contribution to the national economy, which is LO-4's second clause. Not C-2.1-LO-13, since no raw-material classification is at issue.
The 4:2:1 ratio of iron ore, coking coal and limestone: a technical process fact. LO-13 would need the industry classified by raw-material source, which this item does not ask.

Prime location factors for an aluminium smelter (bauxite plus regular, assured electricity). LO-17 covers location factors only for jute and sugar, so this analysis of a mineral-based plant's siting sits at the competency level.
The National Jute Policy of 2005 belongs to the jute industry described by LO-17. Not LO-16, which is about agro-based industries as a range and their crop dependence.
India's per capita steel consumption is the chapter's measure of how far the industry has carried the national economy, LO-4. Not C-2.1-LO-14, which asks the basic/consumer distinction.
Which factors are NOT needed to site an iron and steel plant: locational analysis for a mineral-based industry, which LO-17 does not cover (it is jute and sugar only).
Causes of air pollution from industry is LO-5's first clause. Not LO-4, which is about classification and economic contribution.
Where most integrated steel plants are located (the Chhota Nagpur plateau): locational recall. Contrast qid:106053, where the location FACTORS must be reasoned out.
The two prime factors for aluminium industry location: same locational analysis as qid:106050, stated positively.
Where the first cement plant was set up in 1904: historical and locational recall, not a classification or a pollution question.

The states with most cotton textile centres are the cotton-growing states, which is LO-16's point that each agro-based industry follows the output of a particular crop. Not LO-17, which names jute and sugar specifically.
Duplicate stem of qid:106050; prime factors for aluminium smelter location, competency level for the same reason.
Which country has the largest installed spindle capacity: a world ranking. LO-16 is cited where the item turns on an industry's dependence on a crop, which this comparison does not.
The city known as India's electronic capital: locational recall.
Where the first successful textile mill was established: historical recall, as with the cement item qid:106057.
Placing manufacturing in the secondary sector is the classification half of LO-4. Not C-2.1-LO-13 or LO-14, which classify within manufacturing rather than place manufacturing in the economy.
Which air service works for ONGC offshore (Pawan Hans). This is LIFELINES OF NATIONAL ECONOMY content misfiled into Manufacturing Industries; no LO here reaches it, so plain recall is cited.
The meaning of agglomeration economies: an industrial-location term. No LO in this frame defines it, so the recall competency applies.
Which industry has been the major foreign exchange earner: the economic-contribution clause of LO-4, as with qid:106048.
Identifies an electronics industry from a list: recall. LO-13 would require the agro-based or mineral-based classification to be applied, which the item does not ask for.
The negative effect of industrialisation is pollution, LO-5. Not LO-4, which covers the positive contribution to the economy.
The chemical industry is its own largest consumer: a fact about the industry, not a classification or a pollution question.
Sixty per cent of sugar mills concentrated in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar is the sugar-mill location LO-17 names explicitly, alongside jute.
When and where the first successful textile mill was set up: duplicate of qid:106062 with the date added, same recall level.
